newsitem.title: USA: CARBIDE TO UP BUTYL GLYCOL ETHERS CAPACITY.
newsitem.headline: CARBIDE TO UP BUTYL GLYCOL ETHERS CAPACITY.

text.p: Union Carbide Corp said Wednesday it plans to expand butyl glycol ethers capacity at its Texas and United Kingdom plants, both for a February 1998 startup.
Carbide said its Seadrift, Texas, unit will add 65 million pounds to bring capacity to 330 million pounds per year.

The Wilton unit will add 55 million pounds to bring capacity to 105 million pounds for both butyl and methyl glycol ethers. The added Wilton capacity will replace volume that is now toll-converted for Union Carbide at Chocques, France, the company said without naming the processor.

"Worldwide demand for butanol derivatives is strong and growing, especially for butyl glycol ethers which, because of their versatility, are the solvent of choice for many coatings and cleaning product formulations," said James F. Flynn, vice president and general manager, Solvents, Intermediates and Monomers.
Butyl glycol ethers, marketed by Union Carbide as Butyl Cellosolve and Butyl Carbitol solvents, are used as solvents for industrial coatings and hard-surface cleaners.
